section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section focuses on the validation of the K-DOCS, a new measure for domain-specific creativity across five domains: Everyday, Scholarly, Performance, Science, and Art. The present study examined its factor structure, finding a five-factor model consistent across two samples, and investigated the relationship between domain-general traits (including intelligence) and the K-DOCS factors. It also explored the K-DOCS's relationship with the dark triad and its profile structure. Limitations include not capturing the necessity of domain-general traits, not examining environmental factors, and using a general intelligence measure.

section_summary.extract_value: This discussion section focuses on the K-DOCS measure for domain-specific creativity, evaluating its factor structure and validity. The study found a five-factor model for K-DOCS, consistent across two distinct samples: an MTurk sample (n=825) and a Polish sample (N=500). It also investigated the relationship between domain-general traits (such as intelligence and openness to experience) and K-DOCS factors, as well as the dark triad. The section concludes by outlining limitations, including the need for more nuanced intelligence measures, and suggesting areas for future research.
